requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.check`. I did not run them. My conclusion rests on the two supplied tests, the helpers they use, and the reference listing for the sub-requirements.

**Obligations derived from the subject text**
1. `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against the threshold and function rules. It succeeds only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence, and it fails otherwise.
2. It must not build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.

The detailed threshold, function and exception rules are cited sub-requirements. They have their own tests, so I did not reassess them here.

**Mapping to tests**
- **Success path.** In `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]`, a real `habeas test` flow runs on a fixture. The standalone `saved_check`, which runs `habeas coverage-check`, then succeeds and prints "Coverage check passed".
- **Failure path.** The same test adds an `outer` function containing a nested, never-called `hidden` function and a closure. Both the full flow and the standalone `saved_check` then fail. The output reports `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution` and does not report `#fn[outer]: zero execution`. The standalone output says "Coverage check failed". The test also asserts that the saved run's outcome is "success", so the failure comes from the policy and not from the tests.
- **Saved data is unchanged.** The test compares the retained `evidence` files before and after.
- **No model invocation.** `model_tripwire` configures the authoring backend to point at a local TCP listener that counts requests. The test asserts the count is 0 after the full flow and both standalone checks.
- **No build, test or collection.** `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` captures filtered coverage with a test that writes a sentinel marker file. It then runs `coverage-check` with a `cargo` shim on `PATH` that logs its calls and exits 99 on any subcommand other than `metadata`. The command fails with "File execution coverage" output, and the marker file is absent. The forbidden-command log is absent, so no cargo subcommand other than `metadata` ran. The retained coverage files are byte-identical before and after. Together these cover the MUST NOT clauses for building, executing tests and collecting coverage.
- **Exception-accepted success and threshold failure.** The checker's unit tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]` cover these. They include `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report`, `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` and `accepted_exceptions_cannot_waive_invalid_measurement_and_checks_still_collect_errors`. They are marked for `check.exceptions`, `check.threshold`, `check.report` and `check.measurement`, so the "satisfied or accepted exception" composition is tested at the report level.

**Gaps**
I found none that the criteria require reporting. The tests do not drive an exception-accepted pass or a threshold-only failure through the CLI command. However, the command's pass or fail result follows the report those unit tests check, and the CLI tests confirm the command runs read-only against saved data and reports pass or fail.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
